many/many: A detector is a network that looks at an image and draws a box around each object it finds. It rarely draws just one per object: here, two objects come back with four boxes.
many/conf: Each box comes with a confidence: the detector's score for how sure it is that the box holds an object. Here they run from zero to one, and higher means surer.
many/want: One object should get one box. So keep the most confident box, A, and treat a box that overlaps it heavily as the same object, found twice.
many/iou: Heavily means a high IoU, intersection over union. A and B share thirty six squares of the sixty two they cover: zero point five eight.
many/name: The box with the maximum confidence stays, and the overlapping boxes that are not the maximum are suppressed. That is the name: non-maximum suppression.
many/canny: Finding edges needs the same thing. An edge filter answers on the edge and on the pixels beside it. In 1986, John Canny asked for only one response to a single edge, marking it only at the peak.
nms/sort: Non-max suppression runs in rounds. First, sort the boxes by confidence, highest first: A, C, B, D.
nms/keep: Keep the top box, A, and drop every box whose IoU with it is above a threshold, here a half. B, at zero point five eight, is dropped.
nms/stay: C does not touch A, so their IoU is zero, and C stays.
nms/repeat: Repeat with what is left. C is now the most confident, so it is kept, and D, at zero point six three with C, is dropped.
nms/done: Nothing is left to check: two boxes, one per object.
nms/thresh: The threshold sets what counts as a copy. Raise it to zero point six, and B's zero point five eight is no longer above it, so B stays. A higher threshold drops fewer boxes.
chain/row: One case needs care. Here three boxes overlap in a row: C is the most confident, then B, then A.
chain/dropB: C is kept first. B overlaps it at zero point six, above a half, so B is dropped.
chain/ghost: Now A. It overlaps B at zero point five three, also above a half. But B is already gone, and a dropped box drops nothing.
chain/keepA: Only kept boxes count. Against C, the one kept box, A's IoU is zero point two five, so A stays: C and A survive.
chain/why: B was ruled a copy of C and thrown out. A is not a copy of anything still kept, so nothing removes it.
chain/rcnn: In 2014, the R C N N detector of Ross Girshick and colleagues put the rule this way: reject a box whose IoU with a higher scoring selected box is larger than the threshold. Selected means kept.
chain/table: Practice gives the overlaps as a table, rows and columns in letter order. Row B, column C holds the IoU of B and C: zero point six.
chain/first: So start with the row of the most confident box: here row C, not row A.
